coverage.evidence: Universe: 96 cell lines (M1 x four axes x file). Examined 92. Dynamic census in out/ltw2.txt (h_loop_thread_work.py, all-features arm, per-thread profilers): 69 files on the loop thread, 17 on executor threads. Dedicated harnesses ran diagnosis.py, whatif.py, debugger.py, services.py's simulate call and process_worker.py (h_diagnose_refresh, h_whatif_backlog, h_whatif_loop_block, h_gil_hold). Static census, one row per file on the four axes, in out/census.txt (h_cell_census.py). The 13 user-action-only files carry no solve, simulation or executor marker and are not entered by an all-features cycle. The card's server cost is the simulate service (D9-s1-03). Not reached: four cycle-path files whose feature no rig enabled. Their static census is zero on solve, simulation and executor, but their loop_thread_work is unmeasured. C1: re-taken in a quiet window (load1 1.9, out/gil_quiet.txt; h_gil_hold.py --reps 5). Idle null 3.8 ms median. Shipped process route 1.4/1.9 ms median. In-process fallback 11.4/7.3 ms. Three further re-takes at load1 5.3-5.9 agree in direction. C2: card what-if 3 solves, debugger smoke 1, fuse 3, tile 1 or 3, diagnose 2-4 (D9-s1-01), burst D9-s1-03. C3: _co_optimize 97 rows/gradient; _commit_runs 27.7-88.4 SSE/njev; _dhw_build and _dhw_coil_wood_forecast 0 SSE; _avoid_priced_switches gate reached, re-solve refused, 0 SSE. findings.title: A diagnose press runs a full coordinator cycle, re-solving the plan to publish an analysis that needs no solve
findings.claim: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_diagnose_interval ends in async_request_refresh(), so every diagnose press (button or service) enters optimizer._multi_start_minimize 2-4 times (a full main solve, plus a price tile when enabled) although the diagnosis is published by _build_data_dict alone; publishing without the cycle enters it 0 times and still publishes insight.last_diagnosis.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py async_diagnose_interval: _await_process(diagnose_record) -> _store_diagnosis -> await self.async_request_refresh(); the refresh is _async_update_data, which always runs async_run_optimization (main solve, price tile rotation, fuse-advisor gate, sensor-advisor ranking, actuation and the learners' steps). The diagnosis itself is read by _insight_view ('last_diagnosis') inside _build_data_dict.

evidence.unit: _multi_start_minimize entries per diagnose press (two_zone_dhw); 2/2/2/3/4 over the five houses
evidence.machine: box B1 container (4 vCPU, shared by three seats), CPython 3.14, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: counts are contention-immune; the per-press CPU beside them (two_zone_dhw 1.73 s, duty 7.55 s host process CPU) was taken at load1 7.5 and is provisional

perturbation.change: on the coordinator instance, async_request_refresh replaced by a publish-only twin (coord.data = coord._build_data_dict(); coord.async_update_listeners(), what DataUpdateCoordinator.async_set_updated_data does)
perturbation.observed_value: 0 entries per press in all five houses; worker jobs 3-4 -> 1 (diagnose_record only); diagnosis_published stays 1

findings.metric_definition: Entries into optimizer._multi_start_minimize between the call and the return of async_diagnose_interval on a coordinator with 3 warm cycles.
findings.phenomenon_property: A user action whose only output is a published figure (not a change to any solve input) must publish by rebuilding the data dict, never by requesting a coordinator refresh, because every refresh re-runs the full solve cycle.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n 'async_request_refresh()' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  # each caller whose state change does not reach SolveRecord inputs is a seam; at the baseline: coordinator.py async_diagnose_interval

null_control.value: diagnose_record_msm=0 in every cell: the diagnosis job itself enters the solver 0 times; every entry comes from the refresh
null_control.note: and the perturbed arm keeps diagnosis_returned=1 and diagnosis_published=1

reproduction_steps: Run the command; read <house>.baseline.msm_per_press and <house>.perturbed.msm_per_press for the five houses (two_zone_dhw, single_zone_dhw, single_zone, two_zone_dhw_tiles, two_zone_dhw_duty).
drop_most_favourable is the mean over the four cells left after dropping the max (4, the duty house): (2+2+2+3)/4.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py async_diagnose_interval: replace await self.async_request_refresh() with self.async_set_updated_data(self._build_data_dict()) (or the sensor-advisor-carrying equivalent); a features.py check that a diagnose press enters _multi_start_minimize 0 times and publishes last_diagnosis.

findings.title: Background what-if solves stack onto the main solve with no per-cycle budget; the fuse-advisor cycle fails B1 by 1.6x
findings.claim: With price tiles and the fuse advisor on, async_run_optimization runs the fuse what-if plus its steady pair (3 full solves) and the price tile (1 or 3) serially after the main solve in the same cycle, with no per-cycle budget. On an install that prices duty switches, the cycle that carries the fuse advisor reaches 690 reference solves of solver CPU against B1's 430 (quiet window; 793 against 388 at load1 6.4). The main solve alone peaks at 301.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py async_run_optimization tail: _best_effort_cycle_step(_maybe_run_fuse_advisor) -> async_simulate(steady=True) -> _await_optimize + whatif.steady_pair (two _held_solve) ; _best_effort_cycle_step(_maybe_refresh_price_tile) -> async_simulate (steady for the cap tile). Each is a full solve of the same configuration as the main one, so its cost scales with the main solve's (2-3x when cycling_cost > 0 and a duty-switch stop is learned), and nothing bounds, defers or spreads them by the cycle's CPU already spent.

evidence.unit: reference solves of solver thread CPU in the worst cycle (tiles_fuse_duty, cycle 0: main + fuse advisor + steady pair + price tile); B1 = 60 Pi-s = 429.6 reference solves at F=5 and reference 27.9 ms
evidence.machine: box B1 container (4 vCPU, shared by three seats), CPython 3.14, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: quiet window (load1 1.2, out/spc3.txt). Loaded runs (load1 6.4-8.7, out/spc1.txt and out/spc2.txt) read 793-806 ref solves with 5-7 of 12 cycles over; quiet reads 1 of 12 over (the fuse-advisor cycle). Provisional until the judge's quiet re-run.
evidence.tolerance: ±15 % (worst cycle 19.29 / 24.54 / 26.77 s host over three runs, 690-806 ref solves)

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:_multi_start_minimize (entries) and heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:optimize_in_process (thread CPU per job, tagged at heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:_await_process by the submitting coroutine: async_run_optimization / _maybe_run_fuse_advisor / steady_pair / _maybe_refresh_price_tile)

perturbation.observed_value: quiet: worst cycle 690.5 -> 301.2 reference solves; cycles over B1 1 -> 0; msm entries per cycle max 14 -> 4 (out/spc3.txt). Loaded: 792.8 -> 376.5, 5 -> 0 (out/spc2.txt).

findings.metric_definition: Sum over one _async_update_data of the thread CPU of every optimize_in_process job it submits, divided by tests/stress.py:reference_solve's CPU; B1 bound = 60 s / (F=5 x reference).
findings.phenomenon_property: A cycle's total solver CPU (main solve plus every background what-if it triggers) stays within B1 whatever optional advisors are on; background what-if solves are budgeted against the CPU the cycle already spent, not run unconditionally after it.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n 'async_simulate(' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py  # the background callers inside the cycle (_maybe_run_fuse_advisor, _maybe_refresh_price_tile) and whatif.steady_pair's two _held_solve

null_control.value: duty arm (same install, no background what-ifs): worst cycle 301.2 ref solves, 0/12 over B1 (quiet). Default arm: 140.4, 0/12. tiles_fuse without duty pricing: worst 36.6 Pi-s, 0/12.
null_control.note: the effect vanishes when the background what-ifs are off, so the overrun is the stacking, not the main solve

reproduction_steps: Run the command; read tiles_fuse_duty.cycle_max_ref_solves, .cycle_max_drop1_ref_solves, .cycles_over_b1_by_ref and b1_budget_ref_solves; compare duty.* (the perturbed arm).
Per-cycle series: tiles_fuse_duty.cpu_series_s against .main_cpu_series_s gives the background share per cycle (quiet cycle 0: 19.29 s total, 2.76 s main).

Leave-one-out over the 12 cycles (reference solves, quiet): min 3.77 s/27.93 ms = 135. Dropping the worst cycle leaves 422.9, just under B1's 429.6. The overrun is the cycle that carries the fuse advisor (weekly) on top of a tile and the main solve; the stacking itself (background share 2-17 s per cycle) is in every tile cycle.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py async_run_optimization's background tail: run at most one background what-if solve per cycle (fuse advisor and price tile alternate, steady pair spread over later cycles), or skip/defer them when the cycle's main solve already spent more than a share of B1; a stress-style check over the tiles+fuse+duty install.

findings.title: User what-ifs queue 3 solves each behind the worker lock: the 3 s limiter has no in-flight guard
findings.claim: async_simulate(steady=True) -- the simulate_plan service the card's sliders call -- submits 3 full solves per what-if, and whatif.limited_answer refuses only on SIMULATE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (3 s) since the last start, never while an earlier what-if is still solving, so K nudges 3 s apart start 3K worker solves for drafts the card has already superseded and a scheduled solve submitted behind them waits for all of them (12.4x its solo latency at K=4, quiet).
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py async_simulate: limited_answer(held, now) checks held.last_at only; held.last_at is set when a solve starts (#1448), then _await_optimize plus whatif.steady_pair's two _held_solve each take coordinator._PROCESS_LOCK in _run_in_process for one full solve. A what-if costs 3 solves (~6.8 s host here, ~34 s Pi at F=5), far above the 3 s interval, so requests overlap and every one is solved in turn; the card shows only the latest answer.

evidence.unit: worker jobs (coordinator._run_in_process entries, one full solve each) started by 4 what-ifs 3.05 s apart; 3 per what-if
evidence.machine: box B1 container (4 vCPU, shared by three seats), CPython 3.14, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread; shipped route: real persistent process worker
evidence.contention_note: The job count is contention-immune. Latency was re-taken in a quiet window (load1 0.8, out/wb3.txt): solo scheduled solve 1.50 s; behind K=1 6.04 s (4.0x); behind K=4 18.5 s (12.4x); with the guard 5.90 s (3.9x). One what-if costs about 4.5 s of worker wall on the host, over the 3 s interval even here. Loaded run (load1 6.8, out/wb2.txt): 9.46x. Provisional.

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:_run_in_process (entries) driven through heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_simulate with heatpump_optimizer.whatif:limited_answer as the gate

perturbation.change: whatif.limited_answer also answers from the held state while another user what-if is in flight (an in-flight guard), in memory
perturbation.observed_value: worker jobs 12 -> 3 (3 of 4 answers rate-limited); scheduled-solve latency ratio 12.4 -> 3.9 (the K=1 level), quiet

findings.metric_definition: Entries into coordinator._run_in_process (each one solve holding _PROCESS_LOCK) started by K concurrent user what-ifs whose frozen clocks are SIMULATE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS + 0.05 s apart.
findings.phenomenon_property: The worker's queue of user what-if solves is bounded by what is in flight, not by a start interval shorter than one what-if's own solve time: at most one user what-if solves at a time, and a superseded draft is not solved.

null_control.value: K=1: 3 jobs, scheduled-solve latency 4.0x solo (one what-if ahead); K=0: solo 1.50 s (quiet)
null_control.note: jobs scale exactly 3 per admitted what-if (K=1: 3, K=4: 12); with the guard K=4 returns to the K=1 level

reproduction_steps: Run the command; compare k1.*, k4.* and k4.inflight_guard.* worker_jobs_started and scheduled_solve_latency_over_solo.
Pi extrapolation (F=5, an assumption): one what-if = 3 solves, ~34 s of worker CPU on a Pi against the 3 s interval; K=4 holds the worker ~160 s ahead of the scheduled solve.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py async_simulate / whatif.limited_answer: an in-flight latch on WhatIfState (answer with the held answer, rate_limited, while a user what-if solves; or cancel-and-replace the queued one); a features.py check that K overlapping what-ifs start 3 solves, not 3K.

findings.title: Every steady what-if runs reference_day's thermostat simulation on the event loop: 384-960 simulate_step per call
findings.claim: async_simulate(steady=True) calls whatif.schedule_days -> HeatPumpOptimizer.reference_day for both sides synchronously on the event loop thread, so each steady what-if (the card's simulate_plan, the fuse advisor, the cap tile) makes 384-960 ThermalModel.simulate_step calls on the loop and blocks it for 6.1-26.9 ms of host CPU (30-134 ms on a Pi at F=5), over B2's 100 ms when the ask sets a weekend comfort level.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py async_simulate: days = whatif.schedule_days(_scratch({})[:2], (scratch, inputs)) if steady; schedule_days evaluates o.reference_day(i) for the live and the what-if optimizer, which for each distinct day type of the week runs _build_comfort_bounds and two _compute_baseline_power passes (simulate_step per step) -- in the coroutine, between the two awaits, never through _await_off_loop. The same function's solves go to the process worker; this model work does not (bug class P10).

evidence.unit: ThermalModel.simulate_step calls on the loop thread per weekend-comfort what-if (384 in the other five steady cells); loop CPU inside schedule_days 26.9 ms host in the quiet window (median of 3), 0.98 reference solves against B2's 0.73 = 100 ms/(F x 27.5 ms)
evidence.machine: box B1 container (4 vCPU, shared by three seats), CPython 3.14, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread; solves on the shipped process-worker route
evidence.contention_note: call counts exact. The CPU was re-taken in a quiet window (load1 1.0-1.1, out/wl3.txt): weekend 26.9 ms CPU = 26.9 ms wall, heartbeat gap 28.3 ms; the other cells 6.1-10.1 ms. Loaded runs (load1 5.4-6.0, out/wl2.txt) read 23.4-23.9 ms. Provisional until the judge's quiet re-run.
evidence.tolerance: exact (count); CPU ±15 % (23.4 / 23.9 / 26.9 ms over three runs)

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model:ThermalModel.simulate_step (calls on the loop thread) and heatpump_optimizer.whatif:schedule_days (loop thread CPU), driven through heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_simulate

perturbation.change: whatif.schedule_days replaced by a twin whose two reference_day evaluations run through coordinator._await_off_loop (the process worker) before the call, in memory
perturbation.observed_value: quiet: loop simulate_step 384 -> 0 (card_target) and 960 -> 0 (card_weekend); loop CPU in schedule_days -> 0; heartbeat gap 10.7 -> 2.1 ms and 28.3 -> 1.8 ms. Second lever: weekend comfort set (more distinct day types) moves the count UP 384 -> 960 and the CPU 9.0 -> 26.9 ms

findings.metric_definition: simulate_step calls and thread CPU on the asyncio loop's thread during one async_simulate(steady=True), solves on the process worker.
findings.phenomenon_property: No model kernel (simulate_step, simulate_trajectory*, a baseline-thermostat walk) runs on the event loop thread; a what-if's every model evaluation goes through the process worker as its solves do.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n 'reference_day\|schedule_days\|_compute_baseline_power' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/whatif.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py  # callers reached from a coroutine without _await_off_loop

null_control.value: async_simulate(steady=False) (the degree tiles' call): 0 loop simulate_step, 0 ms in schedule_days, heartbeat gap 1.9 ms (quiet)
null_control.note: the loop calls vanish exactly when schedule_days is not reached

reproduction_steps: Run the command; read <house>.<cell>.loop_simulate_step_calls, .schedule_days_loop_cpu_ms_median and .longest_loop_gap_ms_median, and the perturbed_offloop.* rows.

Leave-one-out over the six steady cells' loop CPU (ms host, quiet): dropping the weekend cell (26.9) leaves max 10.1 ms (holiday) = 50 ms Pi, under B2. The B2 overrun needs a schedule with more distinct day types, while the loop-side model work itself (384+ calls, 30-50 Pi-ms) is present in every steady cell.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py async_simulate: evaluate both reference_day calls through _await_off_loop (one job returning both) before schedule_days compares them; whatif.schedule_days takes the two (targets, kWh) pairs. A features.py check that a steady what-if makes 0 simulate_step calls on the loop thread.

non_findings.claim: B7: every batched gradient costs n+1 simulate-step-equivalents (97 at n=96, 49 at n=48) in all 9 cells (two-zone DHW, single zone, single-zone DHW, zero-range DHW cap, manual pin, co-opt small pump, three duty-priced cells), and no cell runs a scalar-jac run. Fixed variables drop rows (manual pin: 74). The 97th row is the fused value.

C3, DHW planning loops: the _co_optimize re-solve and the _commit_runs re-solves gradient at <=97 rows. The DHW planner (_dhw_build, _dhw_coil_wood_forecast) makes 0 model calls. _avoid_priced_switches' re-solve was refused before solving in all 3 cells that reached its gate.
non_findings.value: _co_optimize 93.8/86.5 SSE per njev; _commit_runs 27.7-88.4; _dhw_build 0 SSE; avoid gate reached 3x, 0 SSE

non_findings.claim: Default install: 1 optimize and 1-2 _multi_start_minimize per cycle, worst cycle 140 reference solves against B1's 388. With tiles and fuse on but no duty pricing, the worst cycle was 36.6 Pi-s with 0/12 cycles over.

B3: loop-thread CPU per cycle, counting _async_update_data, the 82 entities' state-write reads and their attribute JSON, is at most 0.15 Pi-s against 0.5 s. Perturbation: a doubled _build_data_dict raises loop_ms 11.2 -> 14.1 ms.
non_findings.value: quiet (load1 0.8-1.7, out/ltw3.txt): default 14.4 ms median / 19.1 ms max host, all_features 17.9 / 21.8 ms, tiles_fuse 16.8 / 22.3 ms, so at most 0.11 Pi-s; perturbed _build_data_dict x2 loop_ms 7.3 -> 10.5 ms; idle 0.6 ms. Loaded (out/ltw2.txt): 22.1-22.3 ms median.

non_findings.claim: Over 4 all-features cycles with entity writes, no model kernel ran on the loop thread except the fuse advisor's steady what-if (filed as D9-s1-04).

non_findings.value: loop simulate_* calls per 4 cycles: 384, all under _maybe_run_fuse_advisor > async_simulate

non_findings.claim: Shipped process route: the executor-side GIL cost is pickling, and the longest loop gap sits near the idle null in the same session. Swapping _await_process for the in-process executor raises it.
non_findings.value: quiet (load1 1.9): process longest 1.4/1.9 ms median vs idle 3.8 ms; perturbed (_await_process -> executor) 12.3/7.6 ms, share 0.08/0.09; job 8.9-9.7 KB, reply 28.6 KB, dumps 0.10-0.16 ms, loads 0.13-0.18 ms. Loaded re-takes (load1 5.3-5.9) agree in direction (out/gil2.txt).

non_findings.claim: Full cycle on the shipped route: in the quiet window the longest loop gap across a whole _async_update_data is 5.8 ms median, 6.1 ms max, about 30 Pi-ms against B2's 100 ms.

In-process fallback (#511) holds the GIL 11.4/7.3 ms median (two_zone_dhw / dhw_cap_zero_range) in the quiet window, at most 57 Pi-ms, under B2. The in-run yield optimizer._gil_yield (sleep(0) per evaluation) is inert: as a no-op or as a real 100 us sleep it leaves the hold and the share where they are. Only sys.setswitchinterval(0.0005) moves them (2.7/5.5 ms).
non_findings.value: quiet: thread 11.4/7.3 ms, share 0.062/0.036; noyield 11.7/7.8, 0.060/0.029; si05 2.7/5.5, 0/0.003 (out/gil_quiet.txt). Loaded: yield100us 19.5/20.0 vs thread 21.5/16.6 (out/gil4.txt)

non_findings.claim: The debugger's solver smoke costs one solve per run, as designed.

leads.what: Round-10 redispatch C4 handed to D9-s1, but it is on the retained_bytes axis: ru_maxrss in a subprocess, and a >672-cycle run to observe the _accuracy plateau directly.

Attribute JSON across the 82 entities is 103.5-107.7 KB per cycle (h_loop_thread_work attr_json_bytes, before the _unrecorded_attributes split). Check it against B6's 16 KB per entity and 5 MB/day recorded.

The stress gate prices single solves. It cannot see a cycle stacking background what-if solves on the main one (D9-s1-02), what-ifs queued behind the worker lock (D9-s1-03), or model work in async_simulate on the loop (D9-s1-04).

The refresh a diagnose press requests also re-runs _apply_action, _record_accuracy, _track_realised_peak and _async_save_energy_totals mid-interval, out of the optimisation cadence. Whether this double-pairs accuracy or double-counts energy was not checked (D1's robustness lens).
